overview.text: JavaScript (often called JS) is a dynamically typed programming language widely used to make web pages interactive. Its core language is standardized as ECMAScript, while browser features such as the Document Object Model (DOM)—which scripts can use to respond to clicks or change page content—come from the browser environment, not the core language itself. Unlike statically typed languages, JavaScript does not require variables to have one fixed data type. It also runs beyond browsers: Node.js is a JavaScript runtime used to build network applications and web servers. This lets developers use JavaScript for both browser interactions and server applications.

key_facts.text: JavaScript is also known as JS; its standardized language specification is called ECMAScript.
It is dynamically typed: a variable can be assigned values of different types without declaring one fixed type for it.
In a browser, JavaScript can use browser-provided objects to respond to user events and interact with a page’s DOM.
Node.js is a runtime for JavaScript that can be used to build network applications and web servers.
JavaScript and Java are different programming languages; the similar names do not mean they are the same language.
